idea: Week three, from the story bank: written from the source, then corrected by two independent editors before voicing.
description: Up to 30 June 2026, 41,440 entities in Maharashtra had been recognised as start-ups by DPIIT, the highest of any state and 1.7 times Karnataka's 24,026. Uttar Pradesh (23,678) and Delhi (22,336) were the other states above 22,000. The ratio to Karnataka was also 1.7 in December 2025 and February 2026.

This is a running count of recognitions: recognition is voluntary and some recognised entities have since closed. State totals, not per person. Figures given by the Commerce Ministry in Lok Sabha answers of 3 February and 28 July 2026.
source: Ministry of Commerce and Industry (Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, DPIIT), Government of India, reply to Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 1446 of 28 July 2026 (Startup India Initiative), Annexure-I: State/UT-wise number of entities recognised as startups by DPIIT as on 30 June 2026 (a running total of recognitions; 36 rows, adding up to the 2,40,092 given in the text of the answer; the cards read 35 rows and the map all 36). Earlier counts: Unstarred Question No. 4046 of 17 March 2026 (as on 3 February 2026) and Unstarred Question No. 588 of 3 February 2026 (as on 31 December 2025). Eligibility for recognition was widened by notification G.S.R. 108(E) of 4 February 2026. Recognition is by application (self-certification), and the count includes entities since closed (Unstarred Question No. 2738 of 16 December 2025: 6,385 recognised entities categorised as closed on Ministry of Corporate Affairs data of 11 November 2025). State totals, not per-person figures.
